title: A text or code preview opens scrolled to where the previous file's preview was left
problem: The text, code, font and table previews give their scroll container a per-file id and then wrap it: `div().id(("text-preview", path_id(&entry.path)))....overflow_y_scrollbar()` (src/finder/preview.rs:985-990; same shape at 958-963, 1008-1013, 1053-1057). gpui-component's `Scrollable` wrapper does not use that id. Its own id defaults to the call site (`id: caller_id()`, gpui-component-0.8.1/src/scroll/scrollable.rs:81), its scroll handle is keyed on it (`scroll_handle_for(&self.id, ...)`, scrollable.rs:142, 261-266), and it overwrites the element's id (`.id(content_id)`, scrollable.rs:155). Its doc says the default is wrong for exactly this case: `.id()` is needed when scrollables 'would otherwise share a single scroll position' (scrollable.rs:88-92). The repo already notes the id replacement in src/finder/nu_panel.rs:158-159. Effect: every text preview on a surface shares one scroll offset, and likewise every code preview. When the next file's preview is already cached, so no spinner frame drops the state, it appears at the previous file's offset: view a.rs, view b.rs and scroll it to the bottom, press Up, and a.rs is shown scrolled down instead of from its first line. Arrowing back and forth through already-viewed source files in the gallery, preview pane or Quick Look hits this constantly. Explore mode's scalar view has the same shape (src/finder/explore.rs:764-768).
proposal: In preview.rs move the per-file id onto the wrapper, which has an inherent `Scrollable::id` (scrollable.rs:92): write `.overflow_y_scrollbar().id(("text-preview", super::views::path_id(&entry.path)))` at preview.rs:990, and the same for `font-preview` (963), `code-preview` (1013) and `table-preview` (`overflow_scrollbar()`, 1057); drop the now-useless `.id(..)` before the wrapper. Do the same at explore.rs:764-768, including the crumb depth in the id so each drilled-into string starts at the top. Wrap the text in an inner `div().id("preview-text").test_support()` so UI tests can observe it, as nu_panel.rs:160 and 179 do. If the preview-jump-to-match or preview-page-keys candidates replace these wrappers with handles held on `Finder`, this is covered by resetting the handle when the path changes.
original_test_plan: Headless UI test (tests/basics.rs): write two 400-line files `a.txt` and `b.txt`, open the fixture in list view with the preview pane (Cmd+Shift+P). Select a.txt, then b.txt (both now cached); record `ui.snapshot("preview-text").bounds().origin.y`; `ui.scroll("preview-text", point(px(0.), px(-300.)))` and assert the origin moved up; select a.txt and assert the origin equals the recorded unscrolled value. Before the fix it stays 300 points up.
original_risks: Very low. Scroll state becomes per file and is dropped when the file stops being shown, so returning to a file starts at the top, which is what a fresh preview already does.

verifier.claim_check:
The core claim holds; the explore-mode part and the test plan do not.

**What the code does today**
- `src/finder/preview.rs:985-990` (text), `958-963` (font), `1008-1013` (code) and `1053-1057` (table) put a per-file id on the div and then call `.overflow_y_scrollbar()` / `.overflow_scrollbar()`.
- `gpui-component-0.8.1/src/scroll/scrollable.rs:81` gives the wrapper its own id, `caller_id()` (the call site). `scrollable.rs:142` and `261-266` key the `ScrollHandle` on that id via `window.use_keyed_state`. `scrollable.rs:155` overwrites the caller's id with `(id, "content")`.
- `gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/window.rs:4356-4374` shows `use_keyed_state` keys on the ancestor id stack plus that key. No ancestor of `preview_body` carries a per-file id: `preview_area` (`preview.rs:736-766`), `render_preview_card` (`768-806`), `preview_pane.rs:47-58`, `quick_look.rs:161`, `views.rs:1042-1047` and `1244-1252`.
- So every Text preview on a surface shares one handle, and likewise every Code, Font and Table preview. The offset survives a content change and is only clamped (`gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/elements/div.rs:2529-2538`).
- State is dropped only when a frame does not touch it, i.e. a spinner frame or a different preview kind. Previews are cached, up to 256 entries (`preview.rs:309-316`, `352-357`), so a revisited file draws with no spinner frame and inherits the previous file's offset.
- Outside the gallery, `ensure_preview` runs at selection time (`mod.rs:1725`, `preview.rs:564`), so a small file's first load may also finish before a spinner frame is drawn; I did not confirm this at runtime.
- The author meant per-file state: the ids are per-file, and the Markdown arm, whose `TextView` id is honoured, is per-file (`preview.rs:936`).
- Nothing in `CHANGELOG.md` or `docs/manual.md` describes this, and no test pins it: there are no hits for `text-preview`, `code-preview` or `explore-scalar` in `tests/`.

**Where the candidate is wrong**
1. **Explore scalar (`explore.rs:764-768`)**: same shape, but not reachable by a user. Going scalar to scalar always passes a grid frame (back, then into). Changing file goes through `ExploreState::Loading` (`explore.rs:516-518`) while a `nu` subprocess runs, which draws the spinner (`explore.rs:670-675`). At a scalar the arrow keys do not move to another item (`explore_move` returns true, `explore.rs:535-551`). The crumb depth in the id is unnecessary.
2. **Test plan**: `ui.scroll("preview-text", ..)` cannot work as written. `Ui::scroll` (`tests/common/mod.rs:465-481`) dispatches at `snapshot.bounds().center()`, and `bounds` is the unclipped layout rect (`gpui-base-0.8.1/src/test_support.rs:404`). For a 400-line text the centre is thousands of points below the 240-pt card (`preview.rs:797`), so the event misses the scroll area and nothing scrolls.
verifier.implementation_notes:
All edits are in `preview_body` in `src/finder/preview.rs`.

**1. Move the per-file id onto the wrapper (four arms)**
- Text (985-990): `div().size_full().bg(..).p(..).overflow_y_scrollbar().id(("text-preview", super::views::path_id(&entry.path)))`, then the rest of the chain.
- Code (1008-1013): the same with `"code-preview"`.
- Font (957-963): `v_flex()....overflow_y_scrollbar().id(("font-preview", ..))`.
- Table (1053-1057): `div().flex_1().min_h_0().overflow_scrollbar().id(("table-preview", ..))`.
- Drop the `.id(..)` before the wrapper in each; `Div` implements `ScrollableElement` (`scrollable.rs:231`).
- `Scrollable::id` is inherent (`scrollable.rs:92`), so it wins over `InteractiveElement::id`. It must be called while the value is still a `Scrollable<_>`, i.e. after `.overflow_*scrollbar()`. `(&'static str, usize)` converts to `ElementId`, as today.
- Leave the Markdown arm alone; it is already per-file.

**2. Make it observable to tests**
- Follow `nu_panel.rs:158-160` and `179`: wrap the text child in `div().id("preview-text").test_support().child(text)` in the Text arm, and wrap the `StyledText` the same way in the Code arm.
- Keep the "preview truncated" div as a sibling.
- Add `use gpui_kit::TestSupportExt as _;` as `preview_pane.rs:10` does; `preview.rs` does not call `test_support()` today.

**3. Leave `explore.rs` out**
- The scalar view cannot inherit an offset (see claim_check).
- If it is touched for consistency, only move the id onto the wrapper, with no crumb depth. Pitfall: `.test_support()` at `explore.rs:765` asserts that the element has an id (`gpui-base-0.8.1/src/test_support.rs:353-356`). Removing the div's `.id()` while keeping `.test_support()` panics in test builds; drop or move both together.

**4. Test helper**
- Split `Ui::scroll` in `tests/common/mod.rs:465-481` into `scroll_point(position, delta)` plus `scroll(id, delta)` calling it with the snapshot centre. The file already has `#![allow(dead_code)]`.

**5. Changelog**
- Add a `### Fixed` entry under `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`: a text, code or table preview no longer opens scrolled to where the previous file's preview was left.

**Resulting behaviour**
- Scroll state is per file per surface and is dropped when the file stops being shown, so returning to a file starts at the top, as a fresh preview does.
- Changing the text size on the same file keeps its position, because the id is unchanged.
verifier.test_plan:
Headless UI test in `tests/basics.rs`, in the "the preview pane" section (around 919-966), using `Fixture`, `Ui::open`, `ui.click`, `ui.press(&cmd("shift-p"))`, `ui.select`, `ui.snapshot` and the new `ui.scroll_point`.

1. `Fixture::new("pane-scroll")`. Before `Ui::open`, write `a.txt` and `b.txt` with 400 short lines each. `.txt` yields `Preview::Text`, because `highlight` filters out "Plain Text" (`src/highlight.rs:76`).
2. `ui.click("view-list")`, `ui.press(&cmd("shift-p"))`, `ui.select("a.txt")`.
3. Record `let top = ui.snapshot("preview-text").bounds().origin;`.
4. `ui.select("b.txt")`. Both files are now cached; optionally assert `has_preview_for_test` for both. Assert the origin equals `top`.
5. `ui.scroll_point(top + point(px(20.), px(20.)), point(px(0.), px(-300.)))`. This aims at the first visible lines, not the element centre.
6. Assert `ui.snapshot("preview-text").bounds().origin.y < top.y - px(100.)`.
7. `ui.select("a.txt")` and assert `origin.y == top.y`.

Before the fix, step 7 fails with the origin still about 300 points up. The assertions are relative, so font metrics on Linux do not matter.

I did not run cargo; this review was read-only.
verifier.risks:
Low.
- **Layout**: the inner observed div adds one block-level wrapper around the text. `nu_panel.rs` already does the same, so layout should not change.
- **Ambiguous test id**: if two surfaces in one window show a text preview at once (for example an in-window Quick Look dialog over the preview pane), `"preview-text"` matches twice and tests must scope with `within(..)`.
- **Shared handle across surfaces**: two such surfaces showing the same file already share one handle if their ancestor id stacks coincide. That is unchanged by this fix.
- **Overlap with other candidates**: if preview-jump-to-match or preview-page-keys move these previews to `ScrollHandle`s held on `Finder`, this change is superseded by resetting the handle when the path changes. The test stays valid.
